title: Teitelboim and Oron (2016): CdS SILAR shell growth and final cleaning

conflictPairs.label: Source ambiguity 1
conflictPairs.source_text: Main p.3 describes strong visible emission after only one atomic CdS layer; SI p.3 first injection represents two atomic layers and proceeds through the fifth layer, while describing visible onset after the first shell. These are retained as separate process/observation statements, not silently converted into a measured final layer count.
conflictPairs.resolution: Source wording or condition remains unresolved; no silent correction.

notes: Source-wide method; final numeric shell thickness and exact specimen dosing are unreported. Main first-layer emission observation is not silently equated to the terminal five-layer series.

scopeLabel: All seven main and ten supporting-information pages read as text and actual page images. general_background.title: Successive precursor additions
general_background.summary: Successive precursor additions provide a way to control the supply of species used for surface growth. Alternating access to the needed elements can favour addition to existing surfaces, while precursor reactivity and surface accessibility influence incorporation.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

general_background.title: Destabilizing a particle dispersion
general_background.summary: An antisolvent can solvate a particle's ligand shell less favourably than the original dispersion medium. Reduced solvation can weaken colloidal stability and allow particles to aggregate and separate from the liquid, depending on the ligands and solvent mixture.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
